name: Bright Beginnings Child Care Development Center

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed meatballs to be hot holding at 115F. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and meatballs were reheated to 165. Ensure any TCs item is being hot held at or above 135F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed no sanitizer to be set up upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bottle was set up and tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure a sanitizer soulition is prepared at the proper sanitization level during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Observed no certified food protection manager (CFPM) available during the inspection. Director’s CFPM license expired. She has re-taken the course and passed, but has not taken the exam again. New cook has an expired CFPM and must re-take the course/test. One employee who was not present during the inspection has a valid CFPM. Ensure course and test are retaken before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

On arrival, no reporting agreements or other similar paperwork was available for inspector observation. A copy of the Sangamon County Conditional Employee of Food Employee Reporting Agreement was found and all current employees were at the facility to sign. Signed copies were completed and observed during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria. 

The new dish machine in the facility is of a residential type. During the inspection a pair of attempts were made to see if it could reach critical sanitizing temperatures. Neither the disk used by the inspector nor a Temp Thermolabel indicated critical safety limits were reached. Discussion took place in relation to options moving foreword. Either changing the sanitizing temperature (or booster) setting or sanitizing separately in the three compartment sink would be viable options. It appears that the facility will be looking into changing the procedures at the facility to include the three part sink for sanitizing and drying. The sink was set up for sanitizing today to correct the immediate situation. Inspector will spot check next week to verify which situation has been decided on for the continuing procedure.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. 

1) A container of pasta intended for employee lunch is stored in the Coleman cooler along with milk intended for the children. 2) An employee sandwich is observed on top of containers of foods intended for consumer service in the reach in cooler in the kitchen. Both meals were removed during the inspection to correct the violation. A discussion took place with the PIC in relation to storage of employee personal foods/ drinks in the facility.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the sanitizer solutions shall be provided. 

On arrival there was not a way to verify that the new dish machine reaches the critical temperature of 160F required for sanitizing food contact surfaces. Both temperature test strips and reusable maximum registering thermometers were discussed. A small set of strip were acquired during the inspection to correct the violation. PIC is instructed to ensure that some form of check is available at the facility at all times.
